details: I spent the first 18 years of my life in Portland, Oregon. In high school, I ran cross country and track, eventually leading me to run at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland. I decided on entering JHU as a Mechanical Engineering Major after reading biographies of Warner Von Braun and Elon Musk  during my senior year of High School. I was especially inspired by Warner's description of 'turning forward the wheel of human progress'. This initial interest in aerospace led me involve myself in a few cool opportunities during my freshman year of college, including computational research investigating the formation of magnetic fields in protoplanets and a student-perspective into the development of the VfOx Sensor for NASA's DAVINCI Mission. This all led into my first proper experience in the engineering workforce: a summer internship at Precision Castparts Corp.. At PCC, I got the opportunity to see the behind-the-scenes of what it takes to manufacture large investment castings for jet engines and other turbomachinery structures. It taught me the most valuable skills I've learned in any summer job I've worked: how to work with people and how to approach problem-solvings from real, not ideal, insight. I finished my 2024 summer with two decisions. First, that I cared significantly about the results of my work, and that I wanted to make sure that I found the end product of my life's work to be meaningful (not Defense). Second, running wasn't something that I wanted to commit time to during my next three-years of college.
